description: Probably Not(e) Math Nerd generates a scale from prime-number ratios, equal divisions of the octave and moments of symmetry, quantises the incoming pitch to it, then picks notes by weighted chance.

params.text: Sets how many pitches either side of the quantised pitch can be chosen, 0 to 10, or a share of the whole generated scale when spread is switched to percent.
An attenuverter, -100% to +100%, scaling the voltage at the input it belongs with before that voltage is added to the control's own setting.
Sets the direction of the choice: fully left only pitches below the quantised pitch, centre both directions, fully right only pitches above.
Sets the starting probability across the candidates: at 100% every candidate is equally likely, at 0% the furthest candidate falls to a tenth of the chance, rising linearly towards the centre.
Sets the key the generated scale is rooted on, C through B.
Sets the balance of the weighting across the scale: turned left the more consonant pitches carry the greater weight, turned right the more dissonant ones do.
Shifts the quantised pitch by whole octaves, -4 to +4.
Holds every chosen pitch inside the octave of the pitch at NOTE IN when lit; unlit, chosen pitches land near the incoming pitch.
Makes the KEY input read a volt per octave when lit, so the key can follow a keyboard or another quantiser; unlit, 0-10V spans the twelve keys.
Steps through the algorithm that thins the generated pitches down to the number asked for: none, Euclidean for the most even spread, Golomb ruler for the least even, or Perfect Balance.
Sets the greatest number of pitches the scale may hold, 1 to 115; the thinning algorithm picks which ones survive.
Steps through how a traditional scale is laid over the generated pitches: off, spread so its pattern stretches across them, repeat so it starts again as often as it fits, or nearest neighbour.
Chooses the traditional scale whose pattern is laid over the generated pitches.
Applies the note weights of the mapped traditional scale to the generated pitches as well, so that a fifth outweighs a seventh.
Chooses the prime number, or one of the transcendental numbers pi, e and phi, used to build pitch ratios on that row.
Sets how many powers of that row's number are used, to 10 as numerators and to 5 as denominators; 0 leaves the number out, 3 uses the number, its square and its cube.
Stretches or shrinks every ratio built from that row's number, -50 to 50 cents.
Sets how wide the interval the scale repeats at is, 2 to 5; at 2 it is the ordinary octave of one volt, and at 5 the repeat takes four volts.
Holds a volt per octave at the input when lit, whatever the size of the scale's repeat interval; unlit, a scale with a double-width octave needs 2V to cover all its notes.
Bends the pitch weights from linear at 0% to logarithmic at 100%, which widens the gap between likely and unlikely pitches.
Detunes the chosen pitch by a random amount of as much as 10 cents; a separate button switches that randomisation to a Gaussian distribution.
Sets the chance that the pitch last played is barred from being chosen again; at 100% a pitch never repeats.
Steps through three ways of generating equal pitches: a set number of equal divisions of the octave, or steps of a fixed size in cents, either fitted inside the octave or carried past it.
Sets the number of equal divisions the octave is cut into, up to 300, or in equal-step mode the size of each step, 1 to 300 cents.
Takes only every nth division, 1 to 100, so 113 divisions with a step of 31 give the 1st pitch, the 32nd, the 63rd and so on.
Sets how many times the step pattern wraps past the end of the divisions and starts again, 1 to 100, which brings in more pitches when the step does not divide evenly.
Sets the moment-of-symmetry pattern: how many large and how many small steps, 0 to 20 of each, the ratio of their sizes, 1 to 5, and the number of levels, 1 to 3.
Steps through how the equal divisions temper the generated pitches: off, tempering only the pitches that fall within the threshold, or tempering them all.
Sets how close a pitch must come to an equal division before it is tempered, and how far it moves when it is: at 0% strength it is untouched, at 100% it becomes the equal-division pitch.
Holds the value of the control it belongs with to whole numbers.
Takes the pitch arriving at NOTE IN and makes it the root the generated scale is measured from.
Gives each polyphonic voice its own channel of the TRIGGER input when lit; unlit, every voice is clocked from the first channel.

inputs.text: The pitch to be quantised, a volt per octave; its polyphony sets how many voices the module runs.
Voltage here works the control it belongs with: added to a knob's setting through that knob's attenuverter, or acting as a press of a button.
A trigger here chooses a new pitch; with nothing patched here no new pitch is chosen.
Takes the random number behind the pitch choice from this voltage, 0-10V, instead of the module's own; each polyphonic channel feeds the matching voice.

outputs.text: The chosen pitch as a volt per octave, with the octave shift and any pitch randomness included.
The probability weight of the pitch last chosen, 0-10V.
A 10V trigger each time the chosen pitch differs from the one before.

notes: the quantised output does not move until a trigger arrives at the trigger input; each trigger is what picks the next note.
menu: Quantize Mode — how the incoming pitch is made to fit: Closet for the nearest note, Round Lower for down, Round Upper for up. Closet is the maker's spelling of closest.
Trigger Delay — holds the trigger by five samples, for clocks that arrive before the pitch has settled.
Pitch Grid — the reference lines drawn behind the scale display, one of Off, 100¢, Major Ratios or Minor Ratios.
Save as Scale File — writes the generated scale to a Scala .scl file at a place you choose.
